content:
Julian Moore: we need to align on wait-time histograms for the mixed-workload scheduler dashboards. I can land metrics in PR but need names/labels ppl are ok w/.

Omar El-Sayed: +1. what exactly do we want? I think we need (a) queue depth gauge, (b) queue wait time histogram per class, (c) service time split prefill/decode (but that might exist already).

Felix Schneider: from dashboard side: if it’s a histogram w/ Prometheus buckets I can do p50/p95/p99 w/ `histogram_quantile`. If it’s a summary I’m going to have a bad time :)

Allison Grant: please use histogram, and please use _seconds units and Prom naming. Also: minimal labels. Label explosion will kill us.

Julian Moore: ok histogram it is. current internal naming in runtime is messy though.

Chloe Martin: can we keep it consistent with other runtime metrics? I keep seeing `rw_runtime_*` and `redwood_*` in grafana. which is “correct”?

Caleb Johnson: telemetry side: official guidance is `rw_*` prefix for runtime-exported metrics. `redwood_*` is for platform services. Not perfect but that’s what ingestion expects in some dashboards.

Omar El-Sayed: +1 on `rw_`. For scheduler: maybe `rw_runtime_scheduler_queue_wait_seconds` as histogram.

Julian Moore: naming bikeshed: 
- `rw_runtime_scheduler_queue_wait_seconds`
- `rw_runtime_scheduler_wait_seconds`
- `rw_runtime_scheduler_dispatch_wait_seconds`
- `rw_runtime_request_queue_wait_seconds`

Allison Grant: please include “queue” in name. “wait” alone is ambiguous.

Felix Schneider: also we’ll want per-class split. labels like `queue_class="short"|"long"`.

Sofia Ivanova: prefer `class="short"|"long"` vs `queue_class`? the dashboard panels will say “short queue wait” anyway.

Allison Grant: I’d rather not use bare `class` label. It’s too generic; we already have `class` in other places (and people will add random values later). `request_class` or `workload_class` maybe.

Marcus Reed: +1. we already have a `class` label in some batching metrics. it’ll collide in people’s brains.

Julian Moore: ok label bikeshed: `request_class`, `workload_class`, `traffic_class`, `queue`, `lane`.

Aisha Bello: SRE POV: “traffic_class” is clearest for oncall. But keep it to 2 values max.

Omar El-Sayed: “traffic_class” reads like customer tier. We also have “tier” labels on some stuff.

Chloe Martin: what about `scheduler_class`? like `scheduler_class=interactive|bulk`.

Sofia Ivanova: I’m wary of “interactive/bulk” bc we are literally doing short vs long prompt (prefill heavy). I don’t want to imply product tier or use case.

Felix Schneider: for panels, I’d rather see `short`/`long` than `interactive`/`bulk` bc those terms will get bikeshedded again later.

Allison Grant: keep values `short`/`long` but label name something explicit like `prompt_class` or `request_class`.

Omar El-Sayed: `prompt_class` seems too narrow (in future we might classify by predicted prefill cost not literal prompt tokens).

Julian Moore: classifier uses prompt tokens now + prefill EWMA later, so “request_class” is ok.

Caleb Johnson: +1 for `request_class`. Also: don’t add route/model labels on this histogram. Histograms * x labels = ouch.

Julian Moore: agreed. base labels I’m proposing:
- histogram: `rw_runtime_scheduler_queue_wait_seconds_bucket{request_class="short|long"}`
- gauge: `rw_runtime_scheduler_queue_depth{request_class="short|long"}`
- counter maybe: `rw_runtime_scheduler_dequeues_total{request_class="short|long"}`

Felix Schneider: can we also get “reason” for dequeue? (normal vs forced-fairness) would help validate fairness window.

Marcus Reed: that’s a good point. we have the fairness window + periodic long service. I can add a `dequeue_reason` label but that might explode?

Allison Grant: careful: labels on counters are cheaper than histograms, but still. If `dequeue_reason` is a fixed small enum (like `normal|fairness_override`) that’s fine.

Omar El-Sayed: +1. Then we can do ratio panels: fairness_override rate, and see if it spikes under load.

Aisha Bello: also need a starvation signal. Is max wait time already measured?

Julian Moore: I can add a gauge for “oldest enqueue age” per class: `rw_runtime_scheduler_queue_oldest_age_seconds{request_class=...}`.

Allison Grant: that’s good. gauge not hist.

Chloe Martin: dashboard naming question: do we want to call it “queue wait” or “scheduler wait”? Folks confuse w/ network wait.

Felix Schneider: panel title can be “Scheduler queue wait (enqueue->dispatch)”. Metric name can stay “queue_wait”.

Omar El-Sayed: define semantics in comments: start timer at enqueue into scheduler queue, stop at dispatch to runtime execution (prefill start). That avoids confusion w/ token streaming latency.

Julian Moore: yep. Also a separate hist for “time in execution”? (dispatch->first token) might already exist in request tracing.

Caleb Johnson: we already have `rw_runtime_request_first_token_latency_seconds` but it includes queueing + compute. Splitting will help.

Sofia Ivanova: priority: queue wait hist + queue depth + oldest_age + dequeue_reason counter. service time split we can follow up.

Marcus Reed: ack. I’ll wire `dequeue_reason` counter in scheduler code path.

Julian Moore: ok final bikeshed decisions (unless objections in next ~1h):
- `rw_runtime_scheduler_queue_wait_seconds` (histogram)
- `rw_runtime_scheduler_queue_depth` (gauge)
- `rw_runtime_scheduler_queue_oldest_age_seconds` (gauge)
- `rw_runtime_scheduler_dequeues_total` (counter)
Labels:
- `request_class="short"|"long"`
- `dequeue_reason="normal"|"fairness_override"` on dequeues_total only

Allison Grant: works. please add docstring in code + link to dashboard spec once Felix/Chloe have it.

Felix Schneider: works for me. I’ll build panels using `request_class` split. Please keep buckets sane (don’t do 0.001s increments forever).

Omar El-Sayed: bucket suggestion: `[0.001, 0.0025, 0.005, 0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2.5, 5]` seconds. We care about sub-100ms and also meltdown.

Julian Moore: I’ll copy that. Might tweak to align with other latency hist buckets.

Caleb Johnson: heads up: if you change buckets later it breaks some long-range comparisons. Try to set and forget.

Aisha Bello: +1 set-and-forget. For alerts, oldest_age_seconds is probably the cleanest.

Sofia Ivanova: thanks all. Julian can you post this in the PR description too so reviewers don’t reopen bikeshed?

Julian Moore: will do. :thumbsup:

Chloe Martin: when it’s merged, tag me/Felix and I’ll update the dashboard json templates.

Felix Schneider: +1. also please keep metric names stable; I don’t want to refactor 12 panels because of a rename :)

Julian Moore: no renames. locking it in.

Allison Grant: (reacted :white_check_mark:)

Omar El-Sayed: (reacted :shipit:)
